Dr. Smith is a science teacher. In her lessons, she often asks students to design small experiments. Last week, her class tested how light affects plant growth. They placed three plants in different conditions; one in sunlight, one in a dark cupboard, and one under an electric lamp. After seven days, the plant in the sunlight was tall and green, the plant in the cupboard was yellow, small and weak, and the plant under the lamp was also green and strong. Dr. Smith explained that plants need light to grow, but not all light has the same effect. The students said the experiment helped them understand photosynthesis in a practical way.
